items.followUp: Why do passengers tend to move forward when a moving bus stops suddenly?

rubric.why: Identifies the tendency responsible for the motion.
rubric.description: Explains that passengers tend to keep moving in their original direction due to inertia.
rubric.how: Award for stating inertia and the tendency to continue in a straight line or original direction.

rubric.why: Connects the passengers’ motion to the bus turning.
rubric.description: Explains that the bus turns while the passengers tend to continue in their original direction, so they appear to move outward.
rubric.how: Award for linking the turn of the bus with the passengers’ outward motion.

modelAnswer: Due to inertia, passengers tend to continue moving in a straight line in their original direction.
When the bus turns, they therefore appear to move outward relative to the bus.

items.followUp: Define moment of force and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Gives the defining relationship for torque.
rubric.description: Defines torque as the product of force and the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis to the force’s line of action.
rubric.how: Award for identifying both force and perpendicular distance.

rubric.why: States the required SI unit.
rubric.description: Writes the SI unit as newton metre.
rubric.how: Award for the unit Nm or an equivalent form.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
It is the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
SI unit: newton metre (N m).

items.followUp: State the conditions for a body to be in mechanical equilibrium.

rubric.why: States the condition for translational equilibrium.
rubric.description: The resultant force acting on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award for stating that net or resultant force is zero.

rubric.why: States the condition for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: The resultant torque acting on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award for stating that net or resultant torque is zero.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.
For complete mechanical equilibrium, the resultant torque acting on it must also be zero.

items.followUp: Define efficiency and state whether it has a unit.

rubric.why: Gives the ratio that defines efficiency.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output work (or energy) divided by input work (or energy).
rubric.how: Award for the correct useful-output-to-input ratio.

rubric.why: States the percentage form or the unit status.
rubric.description: Efficiency is commonly expressed as a percentage and has no unit.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is dimensionless or has no unit; also accept the percentage form.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output work to input work.
Efficiency = (useful output work ÷ input work) × 100%.
Efficiency has no unit; it is dimensionless.

items.followUp: Define pressure and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Gives the definition of stress.
rubric.description: Defines stress as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award for stating force divided by area.

rubric.why: States the SI unit of stress.
rubric.description: Writes the SI unit as pascal (Pa), equivalent to newton per square metre.
rubric.how: Award for Pa or N/m².

modelAnswer: Stress is the force acting per unit area of a body.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), which is equal to N/m².

items.followUp: A 4 kg block rests on a horizontal surface. Find the frictional force if the coefficient of friction is 0.25. Take g = 9.8 m/s².

rubric.why: Identifies the relevant data in SI units.
rubric.description: Records mass as 5 kg and uses gravitational acceleration 9.8 m/s² (or an accepted rounded value).
rubric.how: Award for the correct mass and gravitational acceleration.

rubric.why: Selects the friction relationship.
rubric.description: Uses frictional force equal to coefficient of friction times normal reaction.
rubric.how: Award for F = μN or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: Finds the normal reaction on the horizontal floor.
rubric.description: Uses the normal reaction N = mg for a block on a horizontal surface.
rubric.how: Award for substituting the weight for the normal reaction.

rubric.why: Shows the numerical substitution.
rubric.description: Substitutes the coefficient of friction and the calculated normal reaction.
rubric.how: Award for a correct substitution leading to the frictional force.

rubric.why: Gives the final frictional force with unit.
rubric.description: Obtains approximately 29.4 N (or 30 N when g is taken as 10 m/s²).
rubric.how: Award for either accepted result with newtons.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 5 kg, μ = 0.6, g = 9.8 m/s².
On a horizontal floor, normal reaction N = mg = 5 kg × 9.8 m/s² = 49 N.
Formula: F = μN.
Substitution: F = 0.6 × 49 N = 29.4 N.
Answer: The force of friction is 29.4 N (approximately 30 N if g = 10 m/s²).

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts on an area of 2 cm². Calculate the pressure in pascals.

rubric.why: Identifies the force and contact area.
rubric.description: Records the applied force as 75 N and the area as 1.5 cm².
rubric.how: Award for the correct given values.

rubric.why: Converts the area to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts 1.5 cm² to 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m².
rubric.how: Award for the correct area conversion.

rubric.why: Uses the pressure formula.
rubric.description: Uses pressure equal to force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award for P = F/A or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: Shows the correct substitution.
rubric.description: Substitutes the force and converted area into the pressure formula.
rubric.how: Award for the correct numerical substitution.

rubric.why: Gives the final pressure with SI unit.
rubric.description: Calculates the pressure as 5 × 10⁵ Pa.
rubric.how: Award for the correct result with pascal as the unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 75 N, A = 1.5 cm² = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m².
Formula: P = F/A.
Substitution: P = 75 N ÷ (1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²).
P = 5 × 10⁵ N/m².
Answer: The pressure under the thumb is 5 × 10⁵ Pa.

items.followUp: Define derived quantities and give one example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes base quantities from derived quantities.
rubric.description: Defines base quantities as independent quantities that are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.
rubric.how: Award for describing them as independent or not derived from other quantities.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of a base quantity.
rubric.description: Gives a base quantity such as length, mass, or time.
rubric.how: Award for any one valid SI base quantity.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent physical quantities that are not defined in terms of other quantities.
Example: length (mass or time is also a valid example).
